— The reality of month one

You Wanted A Puppy You Could Enjoy Life With.

  • You pictured the walks.
  • The adventures.
  • The evenings curled up together.
  • A dog you could take places without constantly worrying about what they were going to do next.

And then the puppy arrived.

Suddenly your hands are covered in bite marks.

There’s accidents all over the carpet.

You’re losing sleep because of the crying.

They’re pulling towards every dog they see.
Recall works beautifully in the kitchen and disappears the second you step outside.
You’re being told completely different things by breeders, friends, social media, trainers and strangers on the internet.

And beneath all of it sits that horrible little thought:

“Am I getting this wrong?”

You don’t need to spend your puppy’s first year constantly wondering what you should be doing next.

There is a much clearer way through it.

Who is teaching you

I’ve Spent More Than A Decade Helping Owners Fix Problems That Could Have Been Prevented In Puppyhood

I’m Osai, a clinical canine behaviourist, and I’ve spent my career working with dogs and the people who love them.

Over the years I’ve worked with everything from straightforward puppy problems through to serious behavioural cases.

And one thing became very clear to me.

So many of the issues owners struggle with later in life begin with small decisions made during those first few months.

  • Too much freedom too soon.
  • Poor socialisation.
  • Inconsistent boundaries.
  • Accidentally rewarding behaviours they don’t want.
  • Never properly teaching calmness.
  • Building obedience in the house without teaching the dog how to use it in the real world.
The Perfect Puppy Course is the system I wish every owner could follow before those problems ever have the chance to take hold.
It brings together the principles I use every day and gives you a clear roadmap through the most important year of your dog’s life.

06

A Stronger Relationship With Your Puppy

Become someone your puppy trusts, listens to and enjoys working with — while still giving them all the affection, play and adventure that made you want a dog in the first place.

— Why a roadmap

The Biggest Advantage Of Having A Roadmap?

You Can Prepare For Problems Before You Even Know They’re Coming.

When you’re raising your first puppy, you don’t know what you don’t know.

01

You might not realise that allowing your puppy to greet every dog could make loose-lead walking and neutrality harder later.

02

You might not know that too much freedom can contribute to chewing, toilet accidents and an inability to settle.

03

You might think adolescence means your training has suddenly stopped working.

That’s the dog we’re working towards throughout the Perfect Puppy Course.

The Perfect Puppy Course guides you through the journey in order, showing you what matters now, what you’re preparing for next, and how the decisions you make today affect the dog you’ll be living with months from now.

— Real training, real puppies

You Won’t Just Hear Me Explain It.

You’ll See It Happen.

Dog training makes far more sense when you can watch the process.

That’s why the Perfect Puppy Course combines my latest theory and methodology with extensive practical training footage.

You’ll follow my journey raising my own German Shepherd puppy, Reggie, because seeing a puppy develop over time is incredibly valuable.

But you’ll also see my assistant trainers Ben and Holly working with different puppies, giving you more examples of how the same principles can look with different dogs, personalities and challenges.

You’ll see the repetitions.

The adjustments.

The mistakes.

The moments where the puppy doesn’t immediately understand.

And the progression afterwards.

Because your puppy isn’t a perfectly rehearsed demonstration dog either.

— A note from Will

Your Puppy Is Learning Every Single Day.

Whether you deliberately train them or not.

Every time they pull and reach the thing they wanted, they’ve learned something.

Every time they ignore a cue and nothing happens, they’ve learned something.

Every time excitement around another dog is rehearsed, they’ve learned something.

And every time you calmly guide them, reward the right choice, hold a boundary or practise an important skill, they’re learning too.

 

You don’t need to produce a perfect puppy overnight.

You need to make enough good decisions, consistently enough, that the dog in front of you keeps moving in the right direction.

That is exactly what I want the Perfect Puppy Course to help you do.

A year from now, your puppy will be a year older regardless. Let’s make sure you’re proud of the dog they’re becoming.

— Will

Questions

Before You Join

What age should I start the course?

Ideally, you can begin from the moment your puppy comes home. If your puppy is already a little older, that’s absolutely fine. Start with the foundations and progress from there.

My puppy already has some problems. Can the course still help?

Yes. Plenty of owners join because biting, pulling, crate problems, overexcitement or poor recall have already begun. The course helps you address those behaviours while strengthening the foundations underneath them.

Is this suitable for first-time puppy owners?

Absolutely. The course is designed to help you understand both what you’re doing and why you’re doing it, so you can become more confident as your puppy develops.

Does my puppy have to progress at a certain age?

No. Puppies develop at different rates. The course gives you a clear progression while teaching you to work with the puppy in front of you.

Is this suitable for all breeds?

Yes. Your puppy’s breed and individual temperament will influence how you train and progress, but the core principles around learning, communication, obedience, manners and socialisation apply across breeds.

How long do I have access?

You receive lifetime access to the Perfect Puppy Course.

What is the Perfect Puppy Club?

Your purchase includes 30 days access to the Perfect Puppy Club, giving you additional support while you begin implementing the course.

Let’s make sure you’re proud of the dog they’re becoming.
